​

[{"Name":"Rome The Barber","ProfilePicture":"https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/a-/ALV-UjWsaYlPg2g6xXNQvk1ildut7ITT-RZ6H7Gy4_obImdDLQ0OgBukWw=s120-c-rp-mo-ba12-br100","Rating":5,"Description":"Instinct Muay Thai has become much more than a gym for our family.

My wife, my two boys (8 and 12), and I joined Instinct about two months ago with one goal: train together, learn together, and grow together as a family. We came in with some karate and light BJJ experience, but Muay Thai was new territory for us. From day one, we knew we had found the right place.

First, huge respect to Coach Manny—the owner and captain of the ship. Manny is an outstanding leader, communicator, and teacher. He has a way of breaking things down so they’re easy to understand while still keeping the training serious and authentic. I trust his leadership with my kids, my wife, and myself, and as a father, that says a lot.

And every good captain needs a strong crew. Coach Josh, Coach Matt, Coach Nat, Coach Cam, and Coach Lucas all deserve major recognition. Every one of them brings something different to the table, but they all share the same patience, professionalism, attention to detail, and genuine commitment to their students. The drills are practical and easy to follow—we enjoy them so much that we actually take some home and practice them together.

I also started taking private lessons with Coach Josh, and they have been worth every penny. In just a few sessions, he’s given me a level of confidence and understanding that carries over into every class. He’s an exceptional teacher who explains not just what to do, but why you’re doing it. Thanks to his coaching, I feel much more confident with combinations, movement, and technique, and I’ve even been able to help newer students along with certain combinations and drills during class. That’s a direct reflection of the quality of instruction Josh provides.

The biggest thing for me personally has been what Instinct has done for my 8-year-old son, Gio, who has severe ADHD. Finding something that truly holds his attention and gives him a positive outlet hasn’t always been easy. Coach Josh and Coach Matt have been incredible with him. They understand when he needs to be redirected, when he needs to stay moving, and how to keep him stimulated and engaged without making him feel singled out. When Gio is on those mats, he’s locked in. Seeing that as his dad has been huge for me. He constantly asks when his next Muay Thai class is.

Another thing that really stands out is how welcoming and respectful this gym is toward women. My wife will sometimes attend class without me while I’m at work, and she has always felt completely comfortable, respected, and included. There’s never been any intimidation or weird atmosphere—just good coaching, good people, and mutual respect. For women who may be hesitant about walking into a combat-sports gym, Instinct does an excellent job of making everyone feel like they belong.

The atmosphere overall is a huge win. No egos. No intimidation. Just a welcoming, respectful community that feels like a family while still taking Muay Thai seriously.

Whether you’re looking for an incredible workout, practical self-defense skills, a positive outlet for your kids, a welcoming place for women, or you’re planning to compete one day, Instinct Muay Thai is the real deal.

Manny and his coaching staff have built something truly special. Our family came looking for a place to train together—we found a team we’re proud to be part of.

🥊 Five stars all day. PARKING:

[{"Name":"Frankie4BJJ","ProfilePicture":"https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/a-/ALV-UjULzNdw3Kx3A21cK8BamTWHVXeYFxyl9PTpvouiBFWTjLtOg4pDCw=s120-c-rp-mo-ba12-br100","Rating":5,"Description":"So, as my many photos can attest. I like to train. I've been to many schools, and continue to visit friends at other schools. I'm not the best by far, I like to say I'm just really good at getting beat up, but I'm happy to report most of my partners say I'm good, good at getting smashed lol. I call Arise BJJ my home base. I was with a different school for years, but my job took me out of the country for a few years and I came back looking for a new BJJ home. My old school was still there, but as most of us know, if it's not convenient as far as distance to get there, price ranges, and a different feel for management, I had to look for a new school. I visited several, and stopped when I got to Arise. One of the main sell points for me was the blog Michelle posted on the website, go read it, she did a great job and it got me in the door.  Professor Danny "Diesel" is a dad, and Michelle (Purple belt Co-owner) is a mom. I'm a dad, so they understand the needs of a family and Jiu jitsu is a family. They've really brought that feel of family and comraderie to this school.  All levels, ages, and backgrounds walk though the door with a good attitude and the atmosphere here is always welcoming. BJJ has so many benefits, confidence, weight loss, stress management, just Google it and see for yourself.
If you're on the fence, or even thinking about visiting, just come and see for yourself what Arise BJJ and the world of Jiu Jitsu has to offer you. See you on the mats readers, I look forward to getting smashed but always surviving 😉
Oh yes, forgot to mention, very clean, they do this foot cleaning thing you don't see at many places. They have two working bathrooms, good parking, and offer many different hours to train. ","reply_language":"en","reply_posted_at_unix_micros":1779710926000000,"reply_updated_at_unix_micros":1779710926000000,"published_at":"2026-05-19T19:24:45.553795Z"},{"Name":"Adrian Fernandez","ProfilePicture":"https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/a-/ALV-UjVwHWvF52N8XVG1GNoL1bVfsiU76eo4ecNoMbuizeqT-8qMrFQ=s120-c-rp-mo-ba12-br100","Rating":5,"Description":"V3Perform is the kind of gym that ruins all other gyms for you—because once you’ve trained here, nothing else quite measures up. Walking into a big chain gym after V3 is like downgrading from a gourmet steakhouse to a gas station hot dog.

The trainers? Absolute legends. They don’t just know your name—they know when you’re slacking, when you’re sandbagging, and when you need that extra push that makes you question all your life choices (in a good way). They tailor every workout so it fits your body and your goals—then they make modifications that somehow still leave you sore in muscles you didn’t even know existed. It’s like personal training meets bootcamp meets therapy session.

The equipment? Spotless, sturdy, and actually works (which is more than I can say for half the treadmills I’ve met in my life). Attention to detail is everywhere—weights racked neatly, space laid out so you’re not dodging some guy curling in the squat rack, and bathrooms so clean you’d trust them for a protein shake taste test.

The vibe is where V3 really flexes. This isn’t some soulless chain where you’re just another membership number. It’s a small, locally owned business with heart. The people are friendly, the energy is contagious, and somehow you leave drenched in sweat but also weirdly happy about it.

If I hadn’t moved away, I’d still be here every week—grunting, sweating, and pretending I didn’t almost cry during burpees.
